These are the events in a chronological order.

File: The Prologue Arc

Subject: The Fall of Ai Hoshino
Timeframe: 2007 – 2011

    "Before the revenge began, there was a lie that dazzled the world."

This era marked the prelude to the tragedy. It centered on the absolute idol, Ai Hoshino, the center of the group B-Komachi. The narrative began in a rural hospital in Miyazaki, where the gynecologist Gorou Amamiya and his patient Sarina Tendouji passed away, only to be reincarnated as Ai’s twin children: Aquamarine (Aqua) and Ruby.

For a brief, four-year period, the Hoshino family lived in secrecy, balancing the deception of the idol industry with domestic happiness. This period concluded violently with the "stalker incident," orchestrated by a mysterious accomplice, resulting in the murder of Ai Hoshino in her apartment. This event traumatized the twins and planted the seed of vengeance in Aqua, who deduced that his biological father was the one who leaked their address to the killer.

entries.content:
Subject: The Return to Showbiz

Timeframe: High School Admission Era (1st Year)
Duration: ~2 Months
Estimated Dates: April 2023 – May 2023 (Twins’ Age: 16)

Following a timeskip where the twins were raised by Miyako Saitou, this arc chronicled the twins' re-entry into the entertainment industry. While Ruby sought to follow in her mother's footsteps to become an idol, Aqua operated in the shadows, viewing acting solely as a means to secure DNA samples from industry professionals to find his father.

The pivotal event of this era was the filming of the web drama "Sweet Today." It was here that Aqua encountered Kana Arima—a former child prodigy—for the second time. Aqua utilized his acting not as an art, but as a psychological weapon, creating a viral moment that saved the production and proved his manipulative capabilities.

entries.content:
Subject: Love Now and the Cyberbullying Incident
Timeframe: 1st Year, Late Spring
Duration: ~1.5 Months
Estimated Dates: May 2023 – June 2023 (Twins’ Age: 16)

To gain proximity to the producer Masaya Kaburagi, Aqua joined the cast of the reality dating show Love Now. This arc highlighted the dark underbelly of internet fame. The narrative focused heavily on Akane Kurokawa, a theater actress who became the target of a vicious cyberbullying campaign that nearly drove her to suicide.

Aqua intervened to save her life, inadvertently creating a bond that would complicate his quest. In the aftermath, Akane utilized her terrifying profiling abilities to perfectly mimic Ai Hoshino, giving Aqua a glimpse of the "ideal woman" he lost and cementing Akane as a key player in the unraveling of the mystery.

entries.content:
Subject: Tokyo Blade
Timeframe: 1st Year, Fall/Winter
Duration: ~4 Months
Estimated Dates: September 2023 – December 2023 (Twins’ Age: 16)

Considered by many to be the peak of Aqua's acting career, this arc centered on the stage adaptation of the manga Tokyo Blade. It brought together the "acting geniuses" of the generation: Aqua, Akane, and Kana.

The production was a battlefield of ideologies—emotional acting versus technical precision. For Aqua, it was a traumatic confrontation with his past. To perform his role, he was forced to channel the raw PTSD of witnessing his mother's death. This arc resulted in a temporary emotional release for Aqua and a misconception that his father was already dead, leading to a brief, fleeting period where he considered living a normal life.

Subject: The Fracture and the Dark Star
Timeframe: 2nd Year, Summer/Fall
Duration: ~3 Weeks (Trip + Aftermath)
Estimated Dates: August 2024 – September 2024 (Twins’ Age: 17)

The illusion of peace shattered during a trip to Miyazaki for a music video shoot. It was here that the corpse of Gorou Amamiya was finally discovered by Ruby and Akane.

The revelation catalyzed a fundamental shift in Ruby Hoshino. Discovering that her beloved doctor had been murdered triggered her "Dark Star" awakening. She became manipulative and cold, mirroring Aqua’s earlier darkness. Simultaneously, Aqua discovered that his biological father—Hikaru Kamiki—was still alive. The twins' relationship fractured as their methods and goals aligned in purpose but clashed in execution.

Subject: 15-Year Lie
Timeframe: 3rd Year, All Seasons
Duration: ~1 Year (Pre-production to Release)
Estimated Dates: April 2025 – March 2026 (Twins’ Age: 18)

The penultimate chapter of the saga. Aqua orchestrated a massive multimedia project: a biographical film titled 15-Year Lie. The script, written by Aqua based on Ai’s recordings, was designed as a "social murder" weapon to expose Hikaru Kamiki to the world and ruin his life.

The production blurred the lines between reality and fiction. Ruby played the role of her mother, Ai, forcing her to confront the truth of Ai's love. Aqua played the role of the culprit. This arc saw the reconciliation of the twins as they finally revealed their past life identities (Sarina and Gorou) to one another, unifying their resolve for the final act.

entries.content:
Subject: Towards the Stars and Dreams
Timeframe: Post-Graduation / Movie Release
Duration: < 1 Week (Climax)
Estimated Dates: Spring 2026 (Twins’ Age: 18/19)

"The plan required a monster to kill a monster."

The culmination of Aqua’s life. Following the release of the movie and the successful devastating of Hikaru Kamiki's reputation, the physical confrontation occurred. Aqua had long decided that his survival was not compatible with his definition of atonement.

In the final confrontation, Aqua effectively cornered Kamiki. Rather than allowing Kamiki to continue his spree or escape justice, Aqua tackled him over a cliff edge and into the sea. Aquamarine Hoshino died by drowning, taking his father with him into the depths. His death marked the end of the revenge cycle, leaving behind a grieving sister, a liberated industry, and a legacy defined by a singular, sacrificial act of love.

entries.content:
Age 20 (on death)

Occupation: Idol (former Lead singer of B-Komachi), Actress, Fashion Model

Weight: quite thin

Height: 151 cm (4'11")

Appearance: Ai is a strikingly beautiful young woman with a slender build. Her most defining feature is her gradient-colored eyes, which transition from indigo-purple at the top to a soft pink at the bottom. In each eye, she possesses a bright, six-pointed star—a symbol of her immense natural charisma—though these stars can darken depending on her emotional state. Her hair is a rich indigo-purple, often shimmering with pink highlights, and is typically styled in a half-up, half-down look with a side ponytail on the left, secured by a signature bunny hairpin. On stage, she is often seen in ruffled, vibrant pink idol outfits adorned with star and heart motifs.

Personality: Ai is a complex individual who views the world through the lens of "lies." Having grown up in an abusive environment and an orphanage without knowing the feeling of love, she initially felt unqualified to be an idol. She eventually embraced the idea that "lies are the most exquisite form of love," using her stage persona as a way to tell her fans she loved them in the hopes that, one day, the lie would become a reality. Publicly, she appears bright, cheerful, and impeccably charismatic; privately, she is asocial, somewhat clumsy, and often feels like a loner even among her peers. Despite her reckless and impulsive nature—such as the massive risk of raising secret children while maintaining her career—she is deeply devoted to her children's future, constantly worrying about their well-being.

Backstory: Abandoned by her mother at a young age, Ai grew up in an orphanage with no concept of how to love or be loved. She was scouted by Ichigo Saitou of Ichigo Productions, who convinced her that she didn't need to know how to love to be an idol; she just had to be a good liar. She became the center and face of the idol group B-Komachi, skyrocketing them to fame. At sixteen, she became pregnant with twins, Aqua and Ruby. To protect her career and their future, she gave birth in secret and continued her work as an idol-mother, living a double life. This life of secrets reached a tragic peak when a stalker fan, feeling betrayed by her "lies," tracked her down at her home. In her final moments, she finally realized that her love for her children was the first "truth" she had ever felt.

Special Details:

    She possesses two stars in her eyes, whereas her children only inherited one each.

    Her name, Hoshino (星野), contains the characters for "star" and "field."

    Her favorite color and the official glowstick color for her fans is red.

    Her smartphone password was "45510," the initials of the four founding members of the original B-Komachi.

Ai Hoshino - Relationships
Children: Aqua (older twin, former doctor Goro reincarnated) - reserved, never called her "mother," driven to revenge after her death. Ruby (younger twin, former terminally ill fan Sarina reincarnated) - affectionate, yearned for Ai's attention, became an idol following her footsteps.
Ichigo Saitou: Her scout/manager, treated her like a daughter. Went missing after her death to investigate and seek revenge. Now helping Ruby and Aqua.
Fuyuko Niino: Fellow B-Komachi member. Initially warm, became jealous of Ai's popularity. Now obsessed with Ai's memory, will murder anyone who surpasses her.
Hikaru Kamiki: Father of her children, met at Lala Lai. She broke up with him by lying she couldn't love him, though she truly wanted to raise their children together.
Taishi Gotanda: Director who worked with her, earned her trust. She asked him to make a B-Komachi documentary and gave him DVDs for the twins before her death.

Example dialogue: "Idols are objects of worship, you know? They sparkle through the magic of lies. Lies are the most exquisite love, no?"

entries.content:
Abiko Samemija

Age: 22

Ocuppation: Mangaka

Weight: Lean

Height: short

Appearance: Abiko is a short young woman with messy, dark purple hair that features lighter purple highlights. Her eyes match her hair, starting dark purple and fading into a lighter pink near the bottom. Her pupils are pastel pink—almost white—and uniquely shaped like horizontal lines. She has small, faintly colored lips. She tends to dress casually and comfortably; for example, she is known to wear overalls over a dark long-sleeved dress, or a coat paired with a skirt when visiting production and rehearsal sets.

Personality: On the surface, Abiko is the definition of an introvert. She struggles with communication and tends to keep to herself, rarely speaking to her colleagues early in her career. However, beneath this quiet exterior lies a deeply affectionate, sweet, and passionate individual, especially when discussing her art and stories. Because she uses her work as an outlet for her desire to be understood, achieving massive success initially inflated her ego. She began to see herself as infallible, clashing with editors and using her busy schedule to justify difficult behavior. She set impossibly harsh standards that drove away her assistants, causing her to overwork herself in isolation. Deep down, her abrasive behavior is a coping mechanism; she genuinely wishes to form connections with others but struggles to navigate them. Over time, she learns how to compromise and properly collaborate with fellow creatives.

Backstory: Abiko started her career as an art assistant to Yoriko Kichijouji, the creator of the series I'll Go With Sweet Today. Although Abiko was extremely quiet and closed-off during this period, Yoriko recognized the deep emotion and longing expressed through her drawings. Eventually, Abiko struck out on her own and authored the massively popular hit series Tokyo Blade. The sudden and immense success of her work catapulted her to the top of the publishing industry but also isolated her. When Tokyo Blade was picked up to be adapted into a stage play, she initially clashed fiercely with the production team. Offended by what she saw as the mischaracterization of her cast, she threatened to shut the production down entirely unless she was allowed to rewrite the script herself. With gentle guidance and tough love from her former mentor, Yoriko, Abiko eventually stepped out of her shell, faced her communication issues, and successfully collaborated with the play's scriptwriter to craft a production they were both proud of.

Special Details:

    During her high school years, she was a member of the second illustration/art club at Aoshiba High School.

    Her intense perfectionism during the stage adaptation of her work stemmed from a deep, protective love for her characters and a fear of seeing her beloved creation desecrated by corporate interests.

Relationships: Yoriko Kichijouji - Her mentor and friend who helped her open up from being introverted. They clashed over Tokyo Blade's fame affecting Abiko, but reconciled after discussing Abiko's fear of her manga being ruined by adaptations.
Goa - Stage play scriptwriter. Abiko initially disliked his creative direction and nearly had him fired, but after improved communication they collaborated successfully and she loved the final result.

entries.content:
Age: Deceased (Adult, active during the late Shōwa and early Heisei eras)

Occupation: Professional Actress

Weight: Unknown

Height: Unknown

Appearance: Airi possessed a classic, elegant beauty suited for her status as a leading actress. She had chest-length dark hair that she typically wore split on either side of her face. Her eyes were dark and expressive, often complemented by the use of dark-colored lipstick, giving her a sophisticated and mature aura.

Personality: Publicly, Airi was known as a successful and graceful actress, particularly famous for her roles as wholesome protagonists. However, her true nature was far more predatory and manipulative. She was an unfaithful woman who harbored no guilt over her actions, most notably engaging in the prolonged exploitation and molestation of an 11-year-old boy. Later revelations suggested she was also a victim of the industry's "negative chain reaction," having been exploited herself in her youth, leading her to repeat the cycle of abuse to regain a sense of control.

Backstory: Airi was a star talent of the Lala Lai Theatrical Company and the wife of fellow actor Seijuro Uehara. Despite her marriage, she entered into a transactional and abusive relationship with a young trainee, Hikaru Kamiki, when he was only 11 years old. This relationship resulted in the birth of her son, Taiki Himekawa, whom she allowed Seijuro to believe was his own biological child. Her secret was eventually discovered by her husband, which led to a violent domestic tragedy; Seijuro murdered Airi in a cottage in Karuizawa before taking his own life when Taiki was only five years old.

Special Details: * She famously played the female protagonist in a popular "morning drama," cementing her legacy as a top-tier actress.

    Unusually for the time, she retained her maiden name, Himekawa, after her marriage to Seijuro Uehara.

    Her name, Airi, is composed of the characters for "love" (愛) and "pear" (梨).

    Her crimes and the trauma she inflicted on the Kamiki and Himekawa bloodlines serve as the foundational tragedy of the "15-Year Lie."

Example Dialogue:
"Adults should empathize with children? Don't make me laugh. I was treated exactly the same way when I was their age... and nobody came to save me then."

His most striking feature is his aquamarine-blue eyes, which contain a distinct white/light blue six-pointed star in his right eye—a trait shared with his twin sister and late mother. This star is known to shift in appearance, turning pitch black when he is consumed by dark intent or intense calculation. He is frequently seen in his Youtou High School uniform, consisting of a blue blazer with gold trimmings and a red tie, though his attire varies greatly depending on his current acting role or production work.

Personality: Aqua is characterized by an intellectual, cold, and stoic demeanor. He possesses a level of maturity and strategic thinking far beyond his years, often appearing "gloomy" or emotionally distant to those around him. He is a master of psychological manipulation, frequently using his charm and intelligence to steer situations toward his desired outcomes. Despite this ruthless edge, he is fiercely protective of his inner circle, particularly his twin sister, Ruby. He often operates from the shadows, sacrificing his own reputation or happiness to ensure the safety and success of those he cares about.

Backstory: as a reincarnation of the doctor Amamiya Gorou, and Born as the secret son of the legendary idol Ai Hoshino, Aqua’s early childhood was spent in the hidden glow of his mother’s fame. This idyllic life was shattered when he witnessed her brutal assassination at the hands of a stalker. Convinced that the killer had an inside accomplice, Aqua dedicated his life to a singular goal: finding his biological father and exacting revenge. He entered the entertainment industry not for fame, but as a means to gain access to the information and people necessary for his hunt. His journey has taken him from child acting to reality TV and high-stakes theater, all while he meticulously pieced together the puzzle of his mother’s past.

Special Details:

    The Single Star: Unlike his mother, who had stars in both eyes, Aqua only has one in his right eye, symbolizing that he is "half" of her legacy.

Both know they're reincarnated but didn't know each other's past identities until Aqua revealed he was "Sensei" (Gorou) and she was Sarina. Miyako Saitou (Adopted Mother): Former nanny who adopted the twins after Ai's death. Raised him with love; Aqua trusts her with Ruby but earns warnings for his manipulative actions.
Kana Arima: Likes aqua a lot. Met as child actors—he outperformed her, she annoyed him. Reunited in high school; Kana calls him "A-kun," he calls her "Arima." She harbors romantic feelings. He sees her as someone who brings back his old self, calls her "shining like a sun." After dating Akane officially, he avoided Kana to protect her idol career from scandal, revealed Ai's secret to save her reputation. He is confirmed to like Kana. They went on a uniform date; she wants him at her final Christmas performance, dreams of becoming his idol.
Akane Kurokawa: Calls her "Akane" (first name) since before dating. Saved her from suicide during LoveforReal, created video to restore her reputation. Started fake dating, became real after she discovered Ai was his mother and pledged to support his revenge. Dated officially for 6 months—attentive boyfriend who escorted her in rain, replied to texts promptly, patted her head. Akane knows he's smitten with Kana but stayed devoted. He broke up after discovering she was investigating his father independently, not wanting to endanger her. She joined The 15 Year Lie to stop his revenge plan.
Mem-Cho: LoveforReal co-star, later B-Komachi member. Helped save Akane. She talks to him about Kana, teases him for caring deeply about her.
Taishi Gotanda: Boss and mentor since age 4. Works as his assistant. Taishi knows about Ai connection, trained him for acting, wrote The 15 Year Lie script together. She calls aqua "acu-tan"
Taiki Himekawa: Half-brother (same father). Taiki told him not to call him "brother." Co-stars in The 15 Year Lie.
Hikaru Kamiki (Father): Aqua sought revenge believing he leaked Ai's address. Made The 15 Year Lie to expose him. After attempt on Ruby's life, Aqua stabbed himself and dragged Hikaru into the sea, strangling him to death to protect Ruby's reputation.

Despite his heinous actions, he is capable of feigning deep empathy and regret, making him nearly impossible to detect until it is too late.

He later entered a secret, intense relationship with Ai Hoshino at age 15. When the relationship ended and Ai decided to raise their twins alone, Hikaru suffered a psychotic break. He leaked Ai’s secret address to an obsessive fan, leading to her murder. Following her death, he founded his own talent agency and began a years-long spree of targeting talented actresses, seeking to "preserve" their beauty and fame through death.

Special Details:

    Permanent Black Stars: Unlike Aqua or Ruby, whose stars manifest based on emotion, Hikaru’s black stars are a constant feature, signifying a permanent state of deception and malice.

    White Flower Ritual: He has a signature habit of sending bouquets of white flowers to up-and-coming actresses before they meet their "accidental" ends.

    Master of Disguise: As a former prodigy actor, he can flawlessly slip into various roles and personas to manipulate those around him.

    The "Liar's Eye": He possesses the same captivating yet deceptive gaze as Ai Hoshino, which he recognizes instantly in his son, Aqua.

Years Active: 10+ Years (Original) / ~2 Years (Current/New)

Occupation: Idol Group (Ichigo Production)

Current Members: Ruby Hoshino (Center), Kana Arima, Mem-Cho

Original Members: Ai Hoshino (Center), Takamine, Nino, Watanabe, Meimei, Kyun, Ari
Appearance

The aesthetic of B-Komachi has always been defined by a "sparkling, girl-next-door" charm. The Original Generation was characterized by vibrant, multi-colored stage outfits, with Ai Hoshino always at the center as the undeniable focal point. The New Generation carries on this legacy but with a modern twist; their costumes often feature a blend of classic idol ruffles and contemporary fashion, frequently utilizing a white, red, and blue color palette. While the original group relied on Ai’s singular brilliance, the new trio presents a more balanced visual dynamic—Ruby’s "star power," Kana’s refined professionalism, and Mem-Cho’s high-energy influencer aesthetic.
Group Dynamic

    The Original Era: The dynamic was heavily lopsided, with the other six members often feeling like "background dancers" for Ai. This created underlying tension and jealousy, particularly from members like Nino, though they maintained a perfectly polished facade for the public.

    The New Era: This group operates on a "frenemy" foundation. Kana and Ruby are constant rivals who push each other to improve, while Mem-Cho acts as the mature mediator and marketing genius. Despite their bickering, they share a genuine bond forged by their shared underdog status in the industry.

Backstory

B-Komachi was once the flagship group of Strawberry Productions, reaching the heights of the idol world before it was shattered by the murder of its star, Ai Hoshino. The group limped on for two years before officially disbanding. A decade later, Ruby Hoshino—driven by a desire to follow in her mother's footsteps—convinced Miyako Saitou to revive the name. Alongside the "genius child actor" Kana Arima and the popular YouTuber Mem-Cho, the new B-Komachi was formed to finish the dream Ai never could: performing a solo concert at the Tokyo Dome.
Special Details

    The Signature "B": The group's signature hand sign involves forming a "B" with the fingers, usually accompanied by the catchphrase "Your Idol Sign is B!"

    The "45510" Secret: The password to Ai's old blog and phone, "45510," is composed of the keypad initials of the four founding members: Takamine (4), Nino (55), Ai (1), and Watanabe (0).

    Viral Marketing: Unlike the original group which relied on traditional media, the new B-Komachi’s success is largely driven by Mem-Cho’s digital savvy and self-produced social media content.

    Iconic Discography: Their setlist includes "B Is The Sign," "STAR☆T☆RAIN," and "HEART’s♡KISS"—songs that have remained popular for over a decade.

Age: Child (Physical "vessel"), Ancient/Supernatural (True form)

Occupation: Supernatural Guide, Child Actress (Only acted once in the 15 year old lie movie.)

Weight: (Child-like build)

Height: (Approximately the height of a young elementary student)

Appearance: Tsukuyomi inhabits the body of a young girl with an unsettling, otherworldly presence. She has long, stark white hair and large, brown eyes that are almost always wide open, giving her a piercing and "creepy" stare. She is typically seen wearing a black and white school uniform, though in later arcs, she transitions to a black dress reminiscent of funeral attire. Before manifesting in this human form, she often took the shape of a seemingly ordinary crow.

Personality: Enigmatic and mischievous, Tsukuyomi possesses an omniscient-like understanding of the world, though she claims she cannot directly read minds. She is a playful, almost taunting figure who takes pleasure in poking at people’s insecurities to get their attention. Despite her childish appearance, her dialogue reveals the wisdom and cynicism of an ancient entity—described by Director Gotanda as a "twisted adult trapped in a child's body." While she often appears detached, she harbors a secret affection for Aqua and Ruby, viewing them as "cheeky children" she has watched over since their past lives.

Backstory: Tsukuyomi is a supernatural being who claims her current body is a "vessel" born to a non-human mother. Her connection to the protagonists dates back to their previous lives; she was the crow that Gorou and Sarina saved from a net at the hospital in Miyazaki. Since then, she has acted as a silent observer of their journey. Following Ai Hoshino's death, she manifested to guide—and sometimes manipulate—the twins toward their destinies. She was the one who revealed the truth of Gorou's death to Ruby, pushing her toward revenge, and later agreed to act in Aqua's "15-Year Lie" film under the stage name Tsukuyomi.

Special Details:

    Crow Transformation: She is almost always accompanied by or manifests through crows; fans frequently refer to her as the "Crow Girl."

    Mythological Roots: Her stage name comes from Tsukuyomi-no-Mikoto, the Shinto moon deity.

    The Guiding Star: She confirmed to Aqua early on that Ai Hoshino’s soul had completely left the world and was not reincarnated, a pivotal moment in his character arc.

    Acting Talent: Despite her supernatural nature, she possesses a natural, raw talent for acting that rivals Aqua’s childhood performances.

    Aqua Calls her "pest"

Example Dialogue:
"God surely is kind, isn't he? He brought two people who never had a mother in the real sense... and a mother who gave birth to soulless children... together. Perhaps... there's more to that than meets the eye."

Notable Episodes:

Finding someone who lost the most money at a race course
Interviewing people who put mosaics on adult videos
Infiltrating the gag tournament of a sweatshop
Finding someone with the name Pikachu-kun
Cosplay Special (controversial episode)

Shun Yoshizumi (deputy director)
Tetsu Urushibara (director, known for inappropriate questions and old-fashioned/rude behavior)

Age: 18

Occupation: Multi-talented Entertainer (Actor, Singer, Dancer), High School Student

Weight: Undisclosed

Height: 163 cm (5'4")

Appearance: Often described as the definitive "pretty girl," Frill possesses long, waist-length dark-green hair and striking yellow-green eyes with unique, slit-like pupils that give her a cat-like or reptilian gaze. She has a distinctive beauty mark located near the lower right side of her lips. Her presence is that of an "aesthetic model," typically seen in her Youtou High School uniform or high-fashion professional attire.

Personality: Frill maintains an aloof and composed demeanor, often speaking with a blunt but observant honesty. She is highly professional and stays remarkably attentive to the careers of her peers, often recognizing even niche performances by her classmates. Despite her calm exterior, she possesses a dry sense of humor and is known for her immense versatility; she can shift her entire aura and personality to fit any role she is assigned, making her a "five-star" talent.

Backstory: Recognized as a "once-in-a-decade" talent, Frill rose to prominence within the entertainment industry at a very young age. She enrolled in the prestigious Performing Arts Program at Youtou High School to balance her education with her skyrocketing career. As one of the most in-demand stars in the country, she has built a reputation for being the first choice for major film and television projects, often serving as the benchmark for success among her generation of performers.

Special Details: She is one of only three entertainers in the industry currently ranked as a "five-star" talent. She holds a strong personal conviction that actors should be chosen for their qualifications and skill rather than through industry connections or nepotism. Due to her piercing, unique eyes, she is sometimes referred to by fans and peers as a "snake-shaped beauty."

Example Dialogue: "I know you. Weren't you on 'Sweet Today'? I heard about it, so I watched. You were good."

Frill Shiranui - Relationships 
Youtou High School:
Ruby Hoshino: Classmate and friend. Frill showed no particular interest during first meeting as Ruby hadn't made a name yet. Bonded over shared interest in LoveforReal. Often seen bantering with Ruby and Minami. Later worked together on The 15 Year Lie. When casting Ai Hoshino's role, Frill tried her best to set Ruby up for it.
Minami Kotobuki: Classmate and friend. Often seen bantering with Ruby and Frill.
Aqua Hoshino: First met when Ruby was talking about her. Aqua asked Frill to get along with his sister. Frill recognized Aqua from Sweet Today live-action, acknowledged his skill. Later worked alongside each other on The 15 Year Lie.
Showbiz:
Akane Kurokawa: Casually mentioned following LoveforReal because she knows someone from the show—revealed to be Akane. As actors in same industry, they know each other. Official meeting shown during Interpersonal Audition for Ai's role with Ruby. Frill is more in-demand due to connections but admits Akane is the better actor. However, wanting Ruby for the role, she purposely challenged both to eliminate Akane while not wanting the role herself.
Mem-Cho: Expressed interest in seeing more of Mem-Cho during LoveforReal conversation. Met in person as castmates on The 15 Year Lie; Frill revealed she became a fan after Mem-Cho's reality show time. Since became friends, hang out together.
Taiki Himekawa: Worked on multiple projects before The 15 Year Lie. Get along well—he invites her on road trip to show off new car, doesn't take offense when she mocks him in front of others.
Taishi Gotanda: Director of The 15 Year Lie. Can be deduced they've worked together; nothing more known.
Family:
Koromo Shiranui: Elder sister

Age:Mid-30s

Occupation: Former Idol (Founding member of the original B-Komachi)

Weight: Undisclosed

Height: Undisclosed

Appearance: During her peak years as an idol, Nino had a slim figure and long brown hair typically styled with side bangs and a distinctive panda-shaped clip. In her mid-30s, her appearance has changed significantly; she wears her hair much shorter, and her face shows visible signs of aging and the toll of her mental instability. Her eyes are a striking green. When not in public, she is often found in disheveled clothing, living in an unsanitary environment.

Personality: Initially perceived as a somewhat "airheaded" girl who followed the lead of others, Nino harbored a deep-seated and corrosive jealousy toward Ai Hoshino as Ai eclipsed the rest of the group. Following Ai's death, this jealousy curdled into a deranged, fanatical obsession. She transitioned from hating Ai to effectively worshipping her, viewing Ai as a "god" who must never be surpassed. This obsession has left her mentally unstable and devoid of traditional morality, leading her to believe that anyone who threatens Ai’s legacy—even Ai's own daughter—must be eliminated.

Backstory: As a founding member of the original B-Komachi, Nino was part of the group’s rise to fame but grew bitter as she was relegated to the background while Ai became the center of attention. During her idol career, she dated Ryosuke Sugano, the fan who would eventually murder Ai. It was later revealed that Nino played a role in the events surrounding Ai's death and remained a long-term accomplice to Hikaru Kamiki. Over the following fifteen years, she lived in seclusion, fixated on Ai’s old performances and acting as a shadow for Hikaru's machinations. Her descent culminated in an attempt on Ruby Hoshino's life, driven by the belief that Ruby had surpassed Ai.

Special Details:  She kept a poster of the original group in her trash-filled apartment, but scribbled over every member's face except for her own and Ai's.

Example Dialogue: "We can't forgive anyone who surpasses Ai. Not even her daughter."

02:11

Fuyuko Niino - Relationships

Ai Hoshino: Fellow B-Komachi member. Nino had complicated relationship—understood Ai was special and elevated the group but held grudge for becoming center at her expense. Once told Ai to go to hell, seemed to regret it afterwards. According to Akane (via Ruby's research for The 15 Year Lie), Ai tried to be normal friends with Nino. After Ai's death, likely due to Hikaru's manipulation, Nino holds Ai in such high regard she starts killing those she deems to have surpassed Ai.

Ryosuke Sugano: When Nino was active idol, regularly met fans including Ryosuke; they started dating. However, Ryosuke changed his idol to Ai. Unknown if they broke up but were on speaking terms immediately after Ai's death. She told him to die; he complied by hanging himself.

Hikaru Kamiki: Met as B-Komachi fan. Unclear if he manipulated her to become accomplice before Ai and Ryosuke's deaths, but certain he took advantage of Ryosuke's death to convince her. Currently remains his accomplice. He used her to gather info on Ruby and The 15 Year Lie. Convinced to attempt Ruby's murder for surpassing Ai. Attempt thwarted; she revealed Hikaru as mastermind.

Age: 31

Occupation: Screenwriter / Scriptwriter

Weight: Undisclosed

Height: Undisclosed

Appearance: Goa is a young man with medium-length brown hair that reaches his neck and distinct purple eyes. He has a small, notable mole located beneath his right eye. He is typically seen in fashionable, modern attire, often accessorizing with scarves and earrings, which gives him a creative and professional aesthetic.

Personality: Calm, well-mannered, and highly informed, Goa is a dedicated professional who loves the theater from "the bottom of his heart." He is known for his immense skill in adapting existing works for the stage, possessing a deep understanding of what can realistically be translated to a theatrical medium. While he is a fan of the original works he adapts, he is also pragmatic, often making necessary adjustments to ensure the audience leaves the theater smiling. Despite facing high-pressure situations and harsh criticism from original creators, he remains patient and hardworking, genuinely enjoying the intricacies of his craft.

Backstory: Goa established himself as a prominent screenwriter in the industry, particularly known for his work on productions like Smash Heaven. He was hired by producer Sumiaki Raida to write the screenplay for the major stage adaptation of the hit series Tokyo Blade. However, he faced a massive career hurdle when the original author, Abiko Samejima, initially hated his script and demanded his removal. Rather than walking away, Goa eventually collaborated directly with Abiko in a high-stakes, "crunch-time" rewrite. This process allowed the two to reconcile their differences, resulting in a script that satisfied the author's vision while remaining performable on stage.

Special Details: He is a self-proclaimed fan of the works he adapts and puts in the effort to read them thoroughly before writing. He has a close professional relationship with producer Sumiaki Raida, who considers him one of the best in the business. On the opening night of Tokyo Blade, he made it a point to personally engage with the original author to ensure their professional bond was mended.

Sumiaki Raida: Know each other well as colleagues, collaborated on multiple stage productions including Tokyo Blade and Smash Heaven. Extensive collaboration—Raida spoke highly of Goa to Aqua Hoshino and Akane Kurokawa, highlighting Goa's love for theater, patience during script revisions, and how his scripts bring smiles to audiences.

Example Dialogue: "I'm a fan of the original work too, you know. But in theater, we have to make it work within the space we're given."

Personality: Gorou is characterized by a deeply compassionate and dedicated nature. As a physician, he maintains a high level of professional diligence and empathy toward his patients. Outside of his clinical duties, he is a fervent and devoted fan of idols, a passion initially sparked by the wishes of a young patient he cared for. Despite his somewhat cynical or "loner" exterior in a quiet rural town, he possesses immense courage and a protective instinct, willing to confront danger to ensure the safety of those under his care.

Years after Sarina's passing, fate brought the pregnant Ai Hoshino to his rural clinic for a secret delivery. Gorou committed himself to protecting her and her unborn children, but his life was cut short when he was murdered on the night of the delivery by a stalker fan.

Age :56 

Occupation: Founder and Former President of Ichigo Productions, now part-timer in Strawberry Productions after the 15 year old lie movie came out.

Weight: Undisclosed

Height: 175 cm

Appearance: Ichigo is a tall man with a commanding presence. In his prime, he was known for his sharp, spiky blonde hair and a flamboyant sense of style, often seen in high-end suits and almost always wearing sunglasses. In recent years, his appearance has become more rugged and weathered; he has grown out his facial hair and typically wears casual, functional clothing like fishing vests and caps to maintain a low profile.

Personality: Bold, ambitious, and notoriously hot-headed, Ichigo possesses a legendary "eye for talent." He is a shrewd businessman who understands the darker side of the entertainment industry better than most. While he can be cynical and blunt, he harbored a deep, paternal affection for his top star, Ai Hoshino. Following the tragedy fifteen years ago, he became consumed by grief and a cold, calculating desire for vengeance, leading him to isolate himself from society.

Backstory: Ichigo built Ichigo Productions from a small-scale agency into a rising power by discovering and nurturing Ai Hoshino. He functioned as both her manager and a surrogate father figure, even going so far as to coordinate the secret birth of her children to protect her career. However, the night of Ai’s murder broke him. Haunted by his failure to protect her, he abandoned his company and his wife, Miyako, disappearing into the underworld to spend over a decade hunting for the person who leaked Ai's private information to her killer.

Special Details: He is an avid fisherman, a hobby he used as a cover during his years in hiding. Despite his self-imposed exile, he remains a master of information gathering and still possesses deep connections within the industry's less savory circles. He eventually resurfaced to provide critical guidance to those seeking the truth behind the "15-year lie."

Example Dialogue: "Do you have any idea how much effort it took to keep your existence a secret? Don't throw it all away for some half-baked stunt." 

Ichigo Saitou - Relationships
Family:
Miyako Saitou (Wife): Married him after he said she could work with attractive men. Put her in charge of looking after Ruby and Aqua after Ai gave birth. After Ai's death, Ichigo abandoned Ichigo Production, leaving Miyako to take over. He felt bad for Miyako when Ruby approached him for advice. Later revealed he abandoned her to pursue Ai's killer without implicating her.
Ruby Hoshino (Adopted Daughter): Ruby sought him out for answers about her father who killed Ai. Ichigo couldn't answer but refused to tell her names of Ai's contacts, aware it could backfire. Promised to do it if Ruby becomes more famous. At her request, gave advice on becoming popular in entertainment.
Aqua Hoshino (Adopted Son): Both share intense desire for vengeance, spent over a decade searching for the man behind Ai's death. After learning Ichigo was helping Ruby, Aqua approached claiming Ai's killer (Seijuro Uehara) was dead. Ichigo pointed out holes in claim—real killer still around, disturbing Aqua. After Aqua exposed Ai's secret, Ichigo was enraged. Aqua revealed he knew killer's name, asked for Ichigo's help hunting him down.
Friends:
Ai Hoshino: Originally scouted Ai, seeing her potential as captivating idol. Through years together in B-Komachi—hardships, unexpected pregnancy, overwhelming success—began seeing Ai as his own daughter. After her death, devastated, disappeared from idol industry without attending funeral. Left Ichigo Production, spent next decade as recluse searching for clues about man behind her murder, vowing vengeance.

Occupation: Actress, Idol (Center of B-Komachi).

Weight: Undisclosed (Though she often claims to be very light, typically around the mid-40s kg range; formerly joked about as "two and a half cabbages" during her child actor days).

Height: 150 cm (4'11")

Appearance: Kana is a petite and beautiful young woman with chin-length, red hair often styled in a bob with blunt bangs. She has large, expressive red eyes that are considered her most striking feature. Her fashion sense is generally described as cute and trendy, and she is frequently seen wearing berets or other stylish hats to coordinate with her outfits.

Personality: Kana is sharp-tongued, professional, and fiercely competitive, often masking her insecurities with a brash, tsundere attitude. Beneath her prickly exterior lies a sensitive and deeply caring individual who craves validation and fears being abandoned. As a professional, she is known for her adaptability; while she was once an arrogant child prodigy, she has matured into a "useful" actor who can suppress her own presence to let her co-stars shine, a survival mechanism developed during her years of struggling to find work.

Backstory: Once known nationwide as the "Genius Child Actor" who could cry on command, Kana was a household name before she even entered elementary school. However, as she grew older, her popularity waned, and the industry slowly turned its back on her, leading to a decade of struggle where she took any role available just to stay relevant. She eventually joined Ichigo Productions, where she was recruited to become the center of the revived idol group B-Komachi, all while continuing to rebuild her acting career through major stage plays like Tokyo Blade.

Special Details: She is infamous for her "10-second tear" ability. Due to a mishearing of her title "The Genius Child Actor who can lick a crying switch" (or similar variations), she is sometimes jokingly referred to by peers as "The Genius Child Actor who can lick baking soda." She also released a novelty song called the "Bell Pepper Exercise" during her childhood, which remains a source of embarrassment for her. She's deeply in love with Aqua. 

Example Dialogue: "I'll show you... I'll be your star! So you'd better look only at me!" (said to Aqua)

Family:
Mother: Aspiring actress who lived vicariously through Kana. Showed affection when Kana was popular but became toxic and neglectful when her fame dipped. Young Kana believed she had to survive in the industry for happiness to be restored.
Ichigo Production, Inc:
Ruby Hoshino: Aqua's twin sister and idol partner. Rocky start as children on That Was the Start set—Ruby misremembered her nickname, angering Kana. Didn't improve when reuniting as teenagers at Youtou High. Relationship improved after becoming idol partners in B-Komachi. Kana guides Ruby as her senior. Became jealous of Ruby's attention but bottled it up until revealing frustration during The 15 Year Lie filming to help Ruby understand her role. Massive rift occurred; Ruby tried mending but gave up. Reconciled after intense scene where they understood each other—Ruby vowed not to abandon Kana as Ai did.
Mem-Cho: Acts like Kana's mentor and big sister. Knows how to manipulate Kana (convinced her to film room as content by mentioning business expenses). There for Kana during difficulties, like when Aqua avoided her. Kana vents her crush on Aqua to Mem-Cho.
Aqua Hoshino: Met at age three as child actors. She was pompous; he admits wanting to strangle her. After their performance, she was humbled by his superior acting—subconsciously limited herself afterward. Reunited in high school, became friends. She developed romantic feelings after working on Sweet Today when he carried scenes, prompting her to act fully. Cried calling him "jerk" after seeing him kiss Akane on LoveforReal. Tried moving on, fell for Pieyon (secretly Aqua in disguise), vowed to make him like her after discovering truth.
He finds her personality distasteful, admits to Akane she's "always rude," but values her worth and skills. Goes out of his way to help her, amplifying her crush. Forced spotlight on her so she couldn't suppress her acting. After finishing his revenge goal, became warmer. Kana calls him "Aqua" (first name); he calls her "Arima" (family name). They went shopping for trip—Aqua paid, picked white suitcase (her lightstick color), took her to dinner. After dating Akane officially, told Kana first, then avoided her for 6 months to protect her idol career from scandal. Mem-Cho realized he's more obsessed with Kana than vice versa. Akane knows "Aqua is smitten with Kana." He revealed Ai's secret to save Kana from scandal. Told her she's "special to him," causing her to flee embarrassed. After The 15 Year Lie filming, said he has fun whenever she's around, flustering her. She finally asked him out on uniform date where she told him her dream is becoming his idol, wants him at her final Christmas performance.
Miyako Saitou: Manager who handles B-Komachi careers. One of first aware of Kana's Aqua crush—deliberately asked Aqua about Akane in Kana's presence, cheering her up.
Pieyon: Mistook him for pervert, apologized upon realizing his popularity. 
Friends:
Melt Narushima: Close male friend, worked on multiple performances. She limited herself to make him look good in Sweet Today. He trained months to prove himself worthy of her kindness. She dragged him along when Taiki invited her out. He patiently listens to her complain about Aqua/Akane. They rehearse together. Commonly seen reining her in during quarrels with Akane while Aqua handles Akane.
Taiki Himekawa: Respected actor. Told her not to hold back during Tokyo Blade, causing her to smile and unleash full ability. Invited her to eat; she accepted eagerly. Became closer—she's his Kanji teacher alongside Melt ("Main clique"). Akane/Aqua determined to defeat Taiki/Kana duo. Kana teases Akane after learning she was Akane's childhood fan.
Showbiz:
Akane Kurokawa: Fierce rivalry as same-age actresses. First met at rigged audition when Kana's popularity waned. Akane was Kana's fan; couldn't believe rigging. Kana started fight, tarnishing Akane's image of her. Years later, Akane became respected actor. Rivalry intensified after Akane became Aqua's girlfriend via LoveforReal. Both cast in Tokyo Blade—Kana showed off knowledge of Aqua, pointed out he can't do emotional acting. Got jealous when Akane cared for collapsed Aqua. During rehearsals, traded insults requiring Aqua/Melt intervention. Despite rivalry, both respect each other, look forward to performing together, both privately admit the other is "true genius." Rivalry subsided during Takachiho trip—Akane gave Kana costume touch-up, shared hot spring. By The 15 Year Lie, bitterness mellowed, held normal conversations. After filming, Kana saw Akane/Aqua talking, encouraged Akane to reunite with Aqua while revealing her own infatuation. Akane explained she's over breakup, pushed Kana to confess, threatened to pursue Aqua if Kana doesn't act by Christmas.
Yoriko Kichijouji: Author of Sweet Today. Kana admires her as manga fan, was sad about disappointing adaptation. Yoriko holds Kana in high regard for saving adaptation alongside Aqua. Friendly terms.
Masaya Kaburagi: Kana believes he has soft spot, keeps hiring her despite fading fame. Truth: exploiting past fame since she's cheap as freelancer. Sees potential—set up B-Komachi's first Japan Idol Festival concert using connections.
Taishi Gotanda: Cast her in That Was the Start as child actress. Negative opinion suggests he didn't choose her. Advised her to get along with people—she took it to heart, learned matching others' acting to survive industry.

Occupation: Premier Theatrical Company and Talent Agency.

Weight: Heavyweight influence in the Japanese performing arts industry.

Height: Peak prestige; widely considered the top-tier destination for serious stage actors.

Appearance: The company is characterized by high-production-value stage plays, most notably their high-profile "2.5D" adaptations of popular works like Tokyo Blade. Visually, their productions are known for a blend of traditional theatrical discipline and cutting-edge stagecraft. The actors associated with the troupe often carry a distinct "Lala Lai" aura—sharp, professional, and deeply immersed in their roles.

Personality: Lala Lai is defined by an atmosphere of intense artistic pursuit and meritocracy. Unlike agencies that focus primarily on idol-like commercialism, this company prioritizes raw talent and "Method Acting." The culture is described as high-pressure and elite, demanding total commitment from its members. They value the ability of an actor to completely lose themselves in a role, a philosophy often referred to within the industry as the "Lala Lai Method."

Backstory: Founded by Toshirou Kindaichi, the company was built on the foundation of elevating the standards of Japanese theater. Over the years, it became a legendary training ground for the industry's most respected performers. It gained significant notoriety for hosting workshops that shaped some of the biggest names in entertainment, including the late superstar Ai Hoshino. Today, it remains the home of "genius" actors like Taiki Himekawa and the highly-acclaimed Akane Kurokawa, maintaining its status as the pinnacle of the acting world.

Special Details: * The Workshop: Lala Lai's acting workshops are notoriously difficult to enter and serve as a "proving ground" for aspiring talents from other agencies.

    Legacy of Genius: The company is famous for fostering actors who possess "natural talent," often acting as a bridge between the idol world and the world of high-brow drama.

    Competitive Casting: They are known for rigorous internal casting processes where only the most capable actors are granted leading roles, regardless of seniority.

entries.content:
This takes place Before Tokyo Blade 2.5D Stage play
The show features a cast of six high-school-aged celebrities from various branches of the entertainment industry (acting, modeling, and internet personality). The premise involves the cast spending weekends together at various locations to bond, engage in activities, and ultimately decide if they have developed genuine romantic feelings for one another by the season finale.
The Cast

    Aqua Hoshino: An actor who joined primarily to build connections with Producer Kaburagi.

    Akane Kurokawa: A serious, talented actress from the Lala Lai Theatrical Company.

    Yuki Sumi: A charismatic fashion model and the show's "breakout star."

    Mem-Cho: A popular YouTuber and influencer.

    Nobuyuki Kumano: A dancer.

    Kengo Morimoto: An aspiring musician.

The Scandal and Turning Point

The show became the center of a massive national controversy midway through its run. Due to pressure to perform and a lack of screen time, Akane Kurokawa accidentally scratched Yuki Sumi’s face during a heated (but scripted) moment.

The incident was edited by the production team to maximize drama, leading to a vicious "flame war" and cyberbullying campaign against Akane. This culminated in Akane attempting to take her own life, an event that was only narrowly prevented by Aqua Hoshino.
The "Counter-Video" and Recovery

To save Akane's reputation and the show itself, the cast took matters into their own hands. Led by Aqua and Mem-Cho, they compiled raw, unedited footage showing the genuine bond and friendship between Akane and Yuki that the official broadcast had omitted.

The video went viral, shifting public sympathy back toward Akane and turning her into a "tragic heroine" figure. This surge in attention made LoveNow one of the most-watched shows of the season.
The Finale and Outcome

The show concluded with a major romantic "success":

    Aqua and Akane: In the final episode, Aqua Hoshino and Akane Kurokawa officially became a couple. While it began as a "work-oriented" relationship to satisfy the audience and the show's narrative, it remained a significant piece of celebrity news in-universe.

    Mem-Cho's Career: Following the show, Mem-Cho's popularity skyrocketed, eventually leading to her scouted by Strawberry Productions to join the idol group B-Komachi.

    Akane's Transformation: During the show, Akane famously "channeled" the persona of the late idol Ai Hoshino to grab Aqua’s attention, a performance so accurate it stunned both the cast and the audience.

Age: 23 (at time of retirement).

Occupation: Former Idol; Currently Fashion Retail Professional.

Weight: Maintaining a slender, industry-standard physique.

Height: Average for an adult female.

Appearance: Mana has the polished, approachable look of a seasoned professional idol. During her stage career, she was typically seen in coordinated, vibrant group costumes—most notably her blue-accented ensemble during her final festival appearances. She carries herself with a practiced poise that remains even after her transition to private life. She has reddish hair styled in a fringe.

Personality: Mana is a pragmatic realist with a surprising amount of self-awareness. While she is capable of maintaining the bright, energetic persona required for the stage, she is deeply introspective behind the scenes. She is not prone to the delusions of grandeur that often plague young performers; instead, she possesses the humility to recognize true "star power" in others and the decisiveness to walk away from the spotlight when she feels her chapter has closed.

Backstory: Her career began at age seventeen after she successfully passed a massive audition for one of the industry's large-scale sister groups. For six years, she navigated the competitive world of ensemble idols, performing at major venues and multiple iterations of the Japan Idol Festival (JIF). Despite her hard work, Mana eventually realized she was playing the role of a "supporting character" in a sea of hundreds of girls. After witnessing a performance by the revived B-Komachi—specifically the radiant charisma of Ruby Hoshino—she had an epiphany regarding the gap between a professional and a true star. Choosing to leave on her own terms rather than being "aged out," she retired from the entertainment industry two weeks later and found stable employment with a popular clothing brand.

Special Details: * Industry Veteran: Completed six full years in the idol business, outlasting many of her original peers.

    Fan Perspective: Originally an "idol otaku" herself, her professional career was driven by a genuine love for the culture.

    The Catalyst: Her sudden retirement is often cited as a quiet testament to the overwhelming impact the new B-Komachi had on their industry contemporaries.

Example Dialogue: "I’ve been a bit player for six years now. My dream of being an idol came true, and I've done enough. Looking at that girl on stage... I finally see the difference. I'm ready to live a normal life now."

Age: Mid 50s

Occupation: Corporate Professional / Socialite.

Weight: Slender.

Height: Average.

Appearance: Marina is a woman of undeniable elegance and poise. She possesses long, dark hair and sharp, sophisticated facial features that give her the air of someone belonging to the upper echelons of society. She is typically seen wearing high-end professional attire or expensive casual wear, always maintaining a meticulously groomed and composed exterior.

Personality: On the surface, Marina appears to be a radiant and devoted mother to her young children, often seen laughing and enjoying the comforts of a wealthy domestic life. However, beneath this polished veneer lies a profound capacity for emotional detachment. She is a woman who prioritizes her own psychological comfort and stability above all else, possessing the chilling ability to completely excise "inconvenient" or painful memories from her life. Her warmth is selective, reserved only for the life she has built in the present, while she remains cold and distant toward the tragedies of her past.

Backstory: Formerly the mother of a terminally ill child named Sarina, Marina found herself unable to cope with the prolonged suffering and eventual death of her firstborn. As Sarina’s condition worsened in a distant hospital, Marina’s visits became increasingly rare until they ceased entirely, as she chose to focus on her career and her own mental well-being rather than face the reality of her daughter's loneliness. Following Sarina’s passing, Marina moved on with startling efficiency. She remarried and started a "new" family, raising two healthy children in a beautiful home where no traces of her first daughter exist. To her neighbors and friends, she is a success story; to those who know her history, she is a woman who abandoned a dying child to save herself.

Special Details: * Selective Memory: She keeps no photographs or mementos of her first daughter, effectively treating that period of her life as if it never happened.

    The Facade of Bliss: She resides in a high-end residential area, projecting the image of a perfect, happy family to the public.

Example Dialogue: "It’s a beautiful day, isn't it? My children are healthy, my home is full of light... I've finally found the happiness I deserve. There’s really no reason to dwell on the past."

Age: Late 40s (estimated).

Occupation: Senior Producer at "Dot TV!" (Internet TV Station).

Weight: 73 kg (estimated, lean professional build).

Height: 180 cm.

Appearance: Kaburagi is a tall, slender man who exudes the weary energy of a high-level executive. He has straight brown hair, styled so that a long fringe almost completely obscures his left eye. His face is marked by noticeable eyebags—a testament to his "workaholic" lifestyle in the entertainment industry. He is almost exclusively seen in sharp, well-tailored business suits.

Personality: A self-proclaimed "mammonist," Kaburagi is a cold realist who prioritizes profit over artistic integrity. He is perfectly willing to produce a project with poor acting or questionable writing as long as it draws eyes and generates revenue. Despite this cynical outlook, he possesses an uncanny, brilliant eye for raw talent. He is a master of the "long game," using his immense network of actors, investors, and media personnel to orchestrate careers. While he speaks mostly of money, those close to him recognize a deep-seated passion for the industry—he believes that without the "money-men," no art would ever see the light of day.

Backstory: He began his career within the prestigious Lala Lai Theatrical Company, which gave him a foundational understanding of elite acting. Transitioning from the stage to the production side, he climbed the ranks to become a powerhouse producer at Dot TV! He is the architect behind several major cultural moments, including the live-action adaptation of Sweet Today and the viral reality hit We’re About to Fall in Love for Real. Because of his long tenure in the business, he is a gatekeeper of secrets, including the private history of the legendary idol Ai Hoshino.

Special Details: * The Master Networker: His influence is so vast that he can secure a leading role or a high-profile workshop spot with a single phone call.

    Trend-Watcher: He maintains a keen awareness of what the younger generation wants, often influenced by the interests of his own daughter.

    Informant: He uses information as currency, trading industry secrets for talent or leverage in his upcoming productions.

Age: 27 (Currently).

Occupation: YouTuber / Idol (Member of B-Komachi) / Actress.

Weight: Undisclosed (Petite, idol-standard physique).

Height: 155 cm (5'1").

Appearance: Mem-Cho is instantly recognizable by her trademark "devil horn" hair accessories and her vibrant, "Gen Z" aesthetic. She sports a short, dyed-blonde bob (often showing brown roots) and wears cosmetic contact lenses (aqua with pink accents) that enhance her wide, expressive eyes. Despite being the eldest member of her group, her youthful features and petite stature allow her to blend in seamlessly with teenagers.

Personality: On camera, she is the archetype of a high-energy, mischievous influencer—playful, "cat-like," and always chasing the next trend. Off-camera, however, she is surprisingly grounded, mature, and empathetic. As the oldest member of B-Komachi, she often acts as the emotional anchor and mediator for the group. She is highly intelligent regarding internet culture and marketing, possessing a business-savvy mind that contrasts with her ditzy online persona.

Backstory: Originally an aspiring idol, Mem-Cho was forced to abandon her dreams shortly after high school to support her family when her mother fell ill. She spent her late teens and early twenties working various jobs to pay for her younger brothers' college tuition. By the time her family was financially stable, she had aged past the standard industry cut-off for idol auditions. Refusing to give up entirely, she pivoted to streaming and TikTok, building a massive following of over a million subscribers by adopting a "high school girl" persona. Her participation in the reality show We’re About to Fall in Love for Real caught the attention of Aqua Hoshino, who recruited her into the revived B-Komachi, finally allowing her to debut as an idol.

Special Details:

    Marketing Strategist: She serves as the de-facto social media manager for B-Komachi, utilizing her expertise in algorithms and viral trends to maximize the group's online reach.

    The Age Deception: She famously maintained a fabrication that she was 18 years old for a significant portion of her streaming career. Technically, she does currently attend high school, having returned to complete the education she paused to work.

    Image Color: Her official penlight color in B-Komachi is Yellow.

Example Dialogue: "...So I pitched myself as 'a high school kid (LOL).' I got way more popular than I expected... and picked up tons and tons of subscribers! After that, I couldn't fess up!"

Mem-Cho - Relationships

Family:

Unnamed Brothers: Has two younger brothers. Cares about them greatly—gave up dream of being idol as a young girl, worked various miscellaneous jobs to raise money for them to afford good university.

Ichigo Production, Inc:

Kana Arima: Met when Aqua invited her to join new B-Komachi. Quickly deduced Kana has crush on Aqua. Knowing he's dating Akane (also her friend), found herself conflicted on who to support. Often tries to cheer Kana up.

Ruby Hoshino: Because of Ruby, finally had guts to make dream come true—becoming idol despite her age. Initially competed for center spot since Kana wasn't interested. Both weren't good enough singers to claim it. After watching Kana's "Full Moon" video, both realized and agreed Kana should be center.

Aqua Hoshino: Met during LoveforReal. First interaction not much to note—acted like typical youth to hide truth. Later chatted about gaining popularity, maintaining status quo; commented on Aqua's disinterest in standing out. After show ended, he invited her to join new B-Komachi. After becoming idol, came to Aqua to talk about Kana. When Aqua distanced himself from Kana, told him to see her and cheer her up. Aqua revealed staying away to protect her idol career. She realized Aqua is obsessed with Kana, not vice versa. Later when Aqua stopped avoiding Kana, teased him about it.

Miyako Saitou: When Aqua invited Mem-Cho to join new B-Komachi, her youthful appearance couldn't fool the President. Added by obvious disturbance in body language, confessed true age and whispered it—totally shocked Miyako as she lied by at least more than half a decade. Still managed to join, forming current B-Komachi trio.

Friends:

Yuki Sumi: Particularly close. Often seen together talking, mostly girl talk.

Akane Kurokawa: Very fond of Akane. First character to search for her after she disappears into storm. Indirectly responsible for saving Akane's life—contacted Aqua, prompting him to search for Akane. Conflicted about supporting Akane or Kana in romantically pursuing Aqua because both are her friends.

Frill Shiranui: After LoveforReal appearance, Frill became fan of Mem-Cho. Met in person during The 15 Year Lie script read where Frill revealed fascination with Mem-Cho after reality show. Since became friends, hang out together.

Mimi Yoshizumi

Age: Early-teens

Occupation: Indie VTuber (under the persona "Suzune Komimi") and Cosplayer (under the name "Nekomimi")

Weight: Unrecorded

Height: Petite / Early-teen stature

Appearance:
Mimi is a young girl with fair skin, long black hair styled with side-swept bangs, and braids on both sides. A defining feature of her face is her prominent double fangs. In her daily life, she is almost always seen in "cat-ear" hoodies, featuring distinctive ring piercings in the fabric ears. As her VTuber avatar, Suzune Komimi, she appears with light-colored hair in an asymmetric bob and oversized, baggy clothing.

Personality:
Characterized by her brother as a "shut-in," Mimi is socially withdrawn and struggles to interact with others or arrange professional collaborations without assistance. While she presents a curated image to her fans, she possesses a hidden, volatile side. She is prone to using harsh language and insults in private, a trait that eventually led to a public scandal. Despite these edges, she is deeply attached to her older brother and shows genuine concern for his well-being.

Backstory:
Mimi struggled with traditional schooling, ultimately failing to attend middle school and retreating into a reclusive lifestyle. To provide her with a future, her brother Shun encouraged her to pivot her hobby of cosplay into the digital world of VTubing. Over three years, she rose to prominence as a top-tier "indie" talent, amassing over 300,000 subscribers through daily Let's Play streams. However, her career was largely derailed after a disastrous cosplay event led to the leaking of "hot mic" clips where she was heard swearing and insulting people, shattering her public image.

Special Details:

    Manager: Her career is managed entirely by her older brother, Shun Yoshizumi.

    Social Media: Operates a private Twitter account with the ID =^pmq^=, dedicated exclusively to her cosplay photos.

    Subscriber Milestone: At the height of her popularity, her channel reached approximately 311,000 subscribers.

Age: 18

Occupation: Gravure Model / High School Student (Performing Arts Program)

Weight: Not publicly disclosed

Height: 163 cm (5'4")
Appearance

Minami is a striking young woman known for her distinct fluffy pink hair, which she usually styles with two periwinkle clips on the right side. She has matching bright pink eyes and a curvaceous physique that has made her a natural fit for the gravure industry. In a school setting, she often puts a personal spin on her Youtou High uniform by omitting the standard vest or blazer, favoring a more relaxed look.
Personality

She is the definition of "go with the flow." Minami is exceptionally friendly and social, often serving as the calm, wise anchor to her more high-energy friends. While she is optimistic and cheerful, she possesses a grounded perspective on the industry. Curiously, she speaks with a Kansai dialect, despite actually being from Kanagawa—a quirk that adds to her laid-back charm.
Backstory

A student in the prestigious Performing Arts Program at Youtou High School, Minami has spent her teenage years balancing the demands of academics with a professional modeling career. She is a mainstay in her social circle, forming a close-knit trio with classmates Ruby Hoshino and Frill Shiranui. Beyond her modeling work, she’s proven to be a reliable friend, even stepping into the world of high-effort cosplay to help Ruby with media segments like Dig Deep! One Chance.
Special Details 

    Signature Style: Known for her "elfin" features when in costume, including a memorable appearance in elaborate faun-like horns for a cosplay shoot.

Miyako Saitou

Age: Late 30s to Early 40s

Occupation: President of Ichigo Production, Inc. / Talent Manager

Weight: Not publicly disclosed

Height: 167 cm (5'6")
Appearance

Miyako is a woman of striking presence with radiant skin and rouge-colored eyes. She wears her strawberry-blonde hair at upper-back length, usually styled with bangs swept to the left. In the earlier years of her career, her wardrobe was defined by extravagant, high-fashion pieces that reflected a more vain lifestyle. However, as she transitioned into her role as a business leader and mother, her style shifted toward more practical, casual, and professional attire, symbolizing her grounded and work-driven nature.
Personality

Miyako underwent a profound personal transformation. Initially perceived as shallow and opportunistic—having married her husband, Ichigo, partly for industry connections—she was once prone to impulsive decisions and resentment. However, the responsibility of raising two children in the wake of tragedy forged her into a woman of immense grit, compassion, and loyalty. While she can be a "pushover" when it comes to the whims of her children, she is a sharp, perceptive professional who navigated the cutthroat entertainment industry for over a decade without her husband's help.
Backstory

Originally a housewife married to the founder of Ichigo Production, Miyako's life was upended when she was tasked with being the secret caretaker for the idol Ai’s twin children. Following Ai's untimely death and her husband’s subsequent disappearance, Miyako made the selfless choice to formally adopt the twins, Aqua and Ruby. Despite having little initial experience in executive management, she took the reins of the struggling Ichigo Pro, successfully pivoting the business to keep it solvent for years. She has remained the steadfast pillar of the Hoshino family, balancing the roles of a protective "manager-mom" and a savvy talent scout.
Special Details 

    The "Miyaemon" Moniker: Affectionately nicknamed "Miyaemon" by her daughter, Ruby.

    Early Secret Keeper: She was the first adult to discover that the Hoshino twins possessed adult-level speech and intelligence as infants—though they initially convinced her they were divine incarnations of gods.

    Industry Intuition: Possesses a "sixth sense" for talent and secrets; she was notably the only person to correctly deduce the real age of the influencer Mem-Cho.

Example Dialogue

    "Don't say that like it's easy. If we could, I would. The dream that Ai showed us... isn't an easy thing to forget. The longer I do this job, the more aware I am that miracles don't happen twice."


Family:
Ichigo Saitou (Husband): Married him so she could work with attractive men, only to find herself looking after Ai's twin children. After Ichigo disappeared following Ai's death, Miyako took over management of Ichigo Production, Inc.
They met when Miyako worked nightlife as Minato girl. Ichigo approached, offered her work at Ichigo Production, Inc. After experiencing the dazzling light that was Ai, Ichigo asked Miyako to support him, promising to show her "the most sparkling scenery in this world." Shared dream: having their talent perform at Tokyo Dome.
After decade of not seeing each other since Ai's death, they ran into each other at bar they frequent. Miyako confronted him about dream they shared, believing he'd given up. Later forced Ichigo to return to Ichigo Production, Inc to clean up mess he left, threatening to sue if he doesn't.
Ruby Hoshino (Adopted Daughter): After Ai gave birth to Aqua and Ruby, Miyako put in charge of looking after them in Ai's place. Originally hated it—attempted exposing truth on internet. After intervention from twins, was subdued. After spending time with twins, came to see them as her children. After Ai's death, became foster mother, grew particularly close with Ruby, raised her as own daughter, showing maternal side.
Initially against Ruby becoming idol like Ai but recognized her potential. When Ruby's idol dreams seemed closer to reality, gave full support, told her to become idol under Ichigo Production, Inc. Advised new B-Komachi about idol industry.
Aqua Hoshino (Adopted Son): Took in Aqua after Ai's death but not as close as with Ruby due to Aqua's personality change, closing himself off from others. Regardless, still loved Aqua as own son, treated him as such even if didn't know what he was thinking. During early acting career, berated him for underhanded methods to achieve goals but nonetheless proud of his growth.
Ichigo Production, Inc:
Ai Hoshino: Worked closely with Ai during career, aware of her amazing talent as rising star. Dream Ai showed her and everyone at Ichigo Production, Inc was unforgettable experience tragically cut short. When took in Ai's children after death, didn't want Ruby following same path as Ai but ultimately allowed her to follow dream. Didn't ask them to forget Ai, saying she'd never change that she was their mother—respects her enough to keep memory alive. Stated Ai was unique, would never be anyone like her again.
Mem-Cho: Not seen interacting often but seem to get along very well. After group's first concert, had casual conversation implying to Mem-Cho that Kana has crush on Aqua.

However, the responsibility of raising two children in the wake of tragedy forged her into a woman of immense grit, compassion, and loyalty. While she can be a "pushover" when it comes to the whims of her children, she is a sharp, perceptive professional who navigated the cutthroat entertainment industry for over a decade without her husband's help.
Backstory

Originally a housewife married to the founder of Ichigo Production, Miyako's life was upended when she was tasked with being the secret caretaker for the idol Ai’s twin children. Following Ai's untimely death and her husband’s subsequent disappearance, Miyako made the selfless choice to formally adopt the twins, Aqua and Ruby. Despite having little initial experience in executive management, she took the reins of the struggling Ichigo Pro, successfully pivoting the business to keep it solvent for years. She has remained the steadfast pillar of the Hoshino family, balancing the roles of a protective "manager-mom" and a savvy talent scout.
Special Details 

    The "Miyaemon" Moniker: Affectionately nicknamed "Miyaemon" by her daughter, Ruby.

    Early Secret Keeper: She was the first adult to discover that the Hoshino twins possessed adult-level speech and intelligence as infants—though they initially convinced her they were divine incarnations of gods.

    Industry Intuition: Possesses a "sixth sense" for talent and secrets; she was notably the only person to correctly deduce the real age of the influencer Mem-Cho.

Example Dialogue

    "Don't say that like it's easy. If we could, I would. The dream that Ai showed us... isn't an easy thing to forget. The longer I do this job, the more aware I am that miracles don't happen twice."


Family:
Ichigo Saitou (Husband): Married him so she could work with attractive men, only to find herself looking after Ai's twin children. After Ichigo disappeared following Ai's death, Miyako took over management of Ichigo Production, Inc.
They met when Miyako worked nightlife as Minato girl. Ichigo approached, offered her work at Ichigo Production, Inc. After experiencing the dazzling light that was Ai, Ichigo asked Miyako to support him, promising to show her "the most sparkling scenery in this world." Shared dream: having their talent perform at Tokyo Dome.
After decade of not seeing each other since Ai's death, they ran into each other at bar they frequent. Miyako confronted him about dream they shared, believing he'd given up. Later forced Ichigo to return to Ichigo Production, Inc to clean up mess he left, threatening to sue if he doesn't.
Ruby Hoshino (Adopted Daughter): After Ai gave birth to Aqua and Ruby, Miyako put in charge of looking after them in Ai's place. Originally hated it—attempted exposing truth on internet. After intervention from twins, was subdued. After spending time with twins, came to see them as her children. After Ai's death, became foster mother, grew particularly close with Ruby, raised her as own daughter, showing maternal side.
Initially against Ruby becoming idol like Ai but recognized her potential. When Ruby's idol dreams seemed closer to reality, gave full support, told her to become idol under Ichigo Production, Inc. Advised new B-Komachi about idol industry.
Aqua Hoshino (Adopted Son): Took in Aqua after Ai's death but not as close as with Ruby due to Aqua's personality change, closing himself off from others. Regardless, still loved Aqua as own son, treated him as such even if didn't know what he was thinking. During early acting career, berated him for underhanded methods to achieve goals but nonetheless proud of his growth.
Ichigo Production, Inc:
Ai Hoshino: Worked closely with Ai during career, aware of her amazing talent as rising star. Dream Ai showed her and everyone at Ichigo Production, Inc was unforgettable experience tragically cut short. When took in Ai's children after death, didn't want Ruby following same path as Ai but ultimately allowed her to follow dream. Didn't ask them to forget Ai, saying she'd never change that she was their mother—respects her enough to keep memory alive. Stated Ai was unique, would never be anyone like her again.
Mem-Cho: Not seen interacting often but seem to get along very well. After group's first concert, had casual conversation implying to Mem-Cho that Kana has crush on Aqua.

Appearance

Nobuyuki is a handsome young man with a distinct look characterized by his semi-long, violetish-black hair. He is an open book—someone who doesn't hide his feelings or his true self, even when the cameras are rolling. He is deeply empathetic and attentive, known for stepping in to defend friends during periods of social hardship. He possesses a playful, approachable charm and a natural ability to form deep emotional connections.

Nobuyuki’s profile rose significantly when he participated in the reality dating show LoveforReal. While reality television is often synonymous with manufactured drama, Nobuyuki prioritized sincerity, seeking out genuine bonds with his castmates. His earnest approach ultimately paid off; despite the way the show's producers edited his confession, he successfully began a real-life relationship with fellow participant Yuki Sumi. He has remained a loyal friend to his former co-stars, providing a grounded and supportive presence in their lives even after the production ended.
