    The "Ah-kun" Nickname: He is known for his affectionate social habits, such as giving Aqua Hoshino the playful nickname "Ah-kun."

    Commitment Symbol: He and his girlfriend, Yuki Sumi, are frequently seen wearing matching bracelets to signify their relationship.

    Loyalty: He was one of the most vocal supporters of his colleagues during times of public backlash, prioritizing human connection over industry reputation.

The 15 year old lie is a controversial biographical film produced by Ichigo Productions and Kaburagi’s production committee. It serves as the final act of Aqua Hoshino’s revenge plot, designed to expose the truth behind the life and death of the legendary idol Ai.

Project Inception

Following the explosive public revelation that rising stars Aquamarine and Ruby Hoshino were, in fact, the secret children of the legendary idol Ai, Director Taishi Gotanda of Ichigo Productions moved quickly to capitalize on the media storm. He revived a dormant project originally conceived fifteen years prior: a biographical film titled The 15-Year Lie. The film was pitched not merely as a tribute, but as a "confession" aimed at exposing the true events surrounding Ai's life and her tragic murder.

The Casting Controversy
The role of Ai Hoshino was the most coveted part in the industry. The initial frontrunner was the "acting genius" Frill Shiranui, though the talented Akane Kurokawa was also a strong contender. However, Director Gotanda and Producer Kaburagi ultimately cast Ai’s own daughter, Ruby Hoshino, for the lead. While critics initially saw this as a nepotistic publicity stunt, insiders reported that Ruby secured the role through a raw, aggressive audition that proved she possessed the requisite "star quality" and darkness to portray the real Ai.

The Cast & Crew
The production boasted a star-studded ensemble, incestuously close to the subject matter:

    Ruby Hoshino as Ai Hoshino.

    Aqua Hoshino as Hikaru Kamiki (The perpetrator/father figure).

    Kana Arima as Nino (A former B-Komachi member).

    Mem-Cho as Meimei (A former B-Komachi member).

    Akane Kurokawa as Takamine (A former B-Komachi member).

    Melt Narushima as Dr. Gorou Amamiya (The attending physician).

    Taiki Himekawa as Seijuro Uehara.

    Tsukuyomi (A mysterious child actor) as the Young Hoshino Twins.

The script was penned by Aqua Hoshino himself, aimed explicitly at weaponizing the film to corner his father, the elusive Hikaru Kamiki, who was revealed to be a sponsor of the film—a move seen by many as a daring provocation.

Filming and On-Set Drama
The shoot was plagued by intense psychological strain. Ruby Hoshino initially struggled to separate her own idealized memories of her mother from the complex, flawed human being she was required to play. Reports from the set indicate she suffered severe emotional distress, unable to tap into the necessary grief.

Tensions flared between Ruby and her fellow idol/actress Kana Arima during the filming of the B-Komachi scenes. Arima, known for her adaptability, reportedly antagonized Ruby on purpose to provoke a genuine emotional reaction, a gamble that resulted in a frostiness between the two before culminating in a breakthrough performance by Ruby and a tearful reconciliation.

The Turning Point for the Hoshino Twins
Perhaps the most significant event occurred away from the cameras. During pre-production, the emotional toll of revisiting their mother's history forced a confrontation between the estranged twins. In a private moment that has since become the subject of intense speculation (and which fundamentally shifted their on-set chemistry), Aqua and Ruby reconciled their differences. They emerged from this period of turmoil with a unified front, channeling their shared trauma into the production.

Conclusion of Production
Filming concluded with the harrowing reenactment of Ai's final moments. Witnesses described the atmosphere on set as suffocating, with Aqua and Ruby delivering performances that blurred the line between acting and reality. The film wrapped production as one of the most anticipated and controversial releases in entertainment history, promising to shatter the lies maintained by the industry for a decade and a half. the movie is intended to provoke the killer into the public eye and force a social "execution."

Category: Supernatural / Psychological Manifestation (Shouldn't be mentioned all the time, only appears in Hoshino family members or people acting like them to a scarily accurate degree.)

Overview: A recurring visual motif in the pupils of specific characters, most notably the Hoshino family.

    White/Bright Stars: Represents "Deceptive Charisma." It is the ability to make a lie look like the absolute truth. It draws people in and makes the person impossible to look away from. Ai possessed two bright stars; Ruby eventually manifests them during her peak idol performances.

    Black/Dark Stars: Represents "Malice and Manipulation." These appear when a character is consumed by revenge, obsession, or the darker side of their "lies." Aqua is most frequently seen with a single dark star, while Ruby develops them during her "Dark Idol" phase.

    Lore Significance: The stars are not a literal biological trait but a visual representation of a character's "star power" and emotional state. When a character loses their "drive" or their "lie" is shattered, the stars can fade or disappear entirely.

Aqua and Ruby Hoshino are reincarnated individuals who retained memories of their past lives.
Previous Lives:
Aqua was Gorou Amamiya, a doctor and obsessed fan of idol Ai Hoshino. He was the gynecologist in charge of delivering Ai's twins. On the night of the twins' birth, he was pushed off a cliff by stalker Ryosuke Sugano (manipulated by Hikaru Kamiki) and died.
Ruby was Sarina Tendouji, a terminally ill 12-year-old patient under Gorou's care. She was also an Ai fan who dreamed of becoming an idol. She died from her illness around the same time as Gorou.
Reincarnation:
Both were reborn as Ai's twin children—Gorou became Aquamarine (Aqua), Sarina became Ruby. Neither knew the other's past identity for years. Ruby searched for "Sensei" (Gorou) after reincarnating but was told he'd gone missing.
Identity Reveal:
After Ruby had a breakdown and began pursuing revenge for Ai and "Sensei's" deaths, Aqua revealed he was Gorou by mentioning "Sarina wanted to be an idol in the hospital." Ruby realized Aqua was Sensei and ran into his arms crying.
Complicated Dynamics:
Ruby retained romantic feelings for Gorou from her past life and sees an "illusion of Gorou" when looking at Aqua. However, Aqua only sees her as his precious little sister. In a dream confrontation with his past self, Gorou told Aqua that Ruby is "far too good for someone like Aqua."

Ruby Hoshino

Age: 18

Occupation: Idol (Member of B-Komachi), YouTuber, TV Personality, Actress

Weight: Undisclosed

Height: 158 cm (5'2")

Appearance: Ruby is a striking young woman of average stature who bears an uncanny resemblance to the legendary idol, Ai Hoshino. She possesses orangish-blonde hair, typically styled with a side ponytail on the left, mirroring her late mother's signature look. Her most captivating features are her pink-ruby eyes, which contain distinctive, star-like highlights—a trait that seems to fluctuate in intensity and color depending on her mental state and level of performance. Whether wearing her Youtou High School performing arts uniform or elaborate stage costumes, her visual charisma is often noted to be overwhelming.

Personality: In stark contrast to her calculated and gloomy twin brother, Ruby is extroverted, optimistic, and loud. She is highly communicative and socially aggressive, capable of making connections quickly, though she often lacks a verbal filter. While she utilizes an "airhead" persona to navigate the entertainment industry, she possesses a keen intuition. Her disposition is generally sunny, but she harbors a deep, obsessive drive regarding her family and her career. This drive can lead her to ruthlessness; while she began with a "pure" outlook, she has shown a willingness to utilize manipulative tactics and darken her own character to achieve her goals and find the truth she seeks.

Backstory: Born in secret to the top idol Ai Hoshino and raised within the care of Ichigo Production, Ruby’s early life was marked by the tragedy of her mother’s murder at the hands of a stalker. Raised by her adoptive parents, Ichigo and Miyako Saitou, she sought to follow in Ai's footsteps, eventually reviving her mother's idol group, B-Komachi. Unknown to the general public, Ruby is the reincarnation of Sarina Tendouji, a young girl who died of a terminal illness while under the care of a doctor named Gorou. Now blessed with a healthy body, she lives her second life with a ferocity intended to fulfill the dreams she couldn't achieve previously, all while hunting for the mastermind behind the destruction of her family.

Special Details: Ruby possesses a unique "star quality" that is literalized in her eyes; initially present in her left eye, she eventually awakens a second star in her right eye as her presence in the industry grows. This radiance is a double-edged sword, capable of turning dark and heavy when her emotions spiral. Despite being the daughter of a genius idol, her singing ability was initially quite poor, though her dancing talent and natural ability to attract fans are exceptional.

Example Dialogue: "But this is our first job. I don't want it... to be a lie."

04:17

Ruby Hoshino - Relationships (~650 words)

Family:

Aqua Hoshino (Older Twin Brother): Very overprotective, not wanting her to walk same path that killed their mother. She and friends call him "sis-con" due to this and lengths he goes to prevent her achieving dreams. Often hindered by his presence, annoyed by his personality—like when he puts on face entering dating show, incredibly off-putting for her and colleagues.

As time passes, he becomes more accepting of her wishes, helps her group prepare for gigs. Disguised himself as Pieyon to prevent coordination problems. Closer than one might think but not aware of each other's past life identities initially.

During LoveforReal, Minami asked how she felt seeing kiss scene between Aqua and Akane—said with pout and sad face it was "5 times more awkward than watching kiss scene between siblings on TV," had mixed feelings. When Melt informed her Aqua leaving rehearsals with Akane, became suspicious. Minami suggested lewd things; Ruby initially frantic but became serious, can't imagine brother risking pregnancy with high school girl—would lose all respect if he did.

After talk with Taiki about parentage, noticed positive change in Aqua's demeanor as he offered making breakfast. Ahead of Miyazaki trip, asked Akane what Aqua threatened her with to get such beautiful person to date him. Requested Akane take care of "incompetent" brother, asked when they'd marry, permission to call her big sister.

To save Kana from scandal, Aqua revealed mother's secret to public—significantly strained relationship. Believing him liar like everyone else, said can't think of him as family anymore.

Things didn't improve until Ruby had meltdown believing she brought misfortune to everyone. Aqua overheard Ruby talking about past life while clutching keychain she gave Gorou in previous life. After initial shock, called her "Sarina," revealing he's the doctor from previous lives. Ruby incredibly happy, relieved to learn he reincarnated as brother. Jumped into arms giving deep hug with tears of happiness.

Ruby stated with sadness Ai said idols often lie. Aqua comforted her saying she and Ai are different people, shouldn't chase her shadow, should live own life, no more need to lie. Ruby said lying caused great pain but kept it up as what Ai did, remarked how she has very unpleasant and dirty thoughts, asked if he's fine with Ruby like that. Aqua told her he's always been biggest fan, admired how in previous life despite hospital pain she still dreamt with sparkling eyes, declaring in those moments she was more radiant than Ai.

This restored Ruby's hopeful gaze, restoring original white star on left eye. After washing tears, declared she'll shine more than Ai. Talked about promise from previous lives where Gorou said he'd marry her after turning 16—with playful look stated she's already 16.

Ruby started displaying affection toward Aqua more openly—shown clinging to him in lighthearted mood, noted by Kana as contrasting recent behavior.

For The 15 Year Lie, cast as lovers with kiss scene. Ruby tried getting Aqua to practice scene night prior. Convinced him to act like Goro while she behaved like Sarina, enjoying similar back-and-forth from previous lives. After brief heart-to-heart, Ruby stole kiss from him guised as practicing one they'd eventually share during shooting.

Ai Hoshino (Mother): Biological mother. Even in past life as Sarina, big fan of her and work. Elated when reincarnated as daughter—able to experience dream before goal of becoming idol. Spoiled, demanded mother's attention whenever around. Utilized every moment to fawn over Ai to spoil and dote on her. While alive, Ai reflected on how similar Ruby was to Otaku after Ruby complimented her smell, asked what shampoo she used despite using same ones. After passing, determined to follow footsteps, prayed to tombstone regularly updating her on life.

Ichigo Saitou (Adopted Father): After Ai's death, became distant from family. After becoming idol, Ruby came to him looking for anyone connected to Ai. Promised to tell her if she becomes popular, provided pointers on how to do so. Helps her using connections to get bigger, more popular roles.

Miyako Saitou (Adopted Mother): Was Ruby and Aqua's babysitter, later became adopted mother. Never once tried stopping Ruby from becoming idol, decided to relaunch idol division of Ichigo Production, Inc. just for her to pursue dreams. Thinks of Ruby as own daughter, can't say no to her.

Ichigo Production, Inc:

Kana Arima: Despite long history, only recently started seriously interacting when latter joined idol group. First met as children on That Was the Start film set. Due to Kana's cocky personality, Ruby developed poor opinion. Similarly, Kana disliked Ruby because latter continuously got nickname wrong.

After first meeting, didn't see each other again until high school. Relationship remained relatively poor. Things took drastic turn when Ichigo Production, Inc. began scouting new idol group. After Aqua pointed out Kana is freelancer, Ruby realized potential but hesitant to approach due to bad standing. While willing to swallow pride, Aqua forced to be in-between arranging meeting—ultimately convinced her.

After Kana joined, while still occasionally banter, relationship improved. Kana became sort of mentor figure, teaching about entertainment world ways. Conversely, whenever Kana gets depressed, Ruby regularly cheers her up. Often gossip about Aqua, share dislike for moody personality.

After witnessing acting during Tokyo Blade stage adaptation, Ruby became more understanding of Kana's passion for acting, over time appreciated her B-Komachi involvement. Kana started becoming frustrated over Ruby's growing popularity. When Ruby cast to portray Ai for The 15 Year Lie, Kana gave various acting advice, let Ruby visit on film set.

Things took drastic turn when Kana revealed frustration attempting to get Ruby to understand mother better—damaged relationship. Ruby made attempts to mend but given cold shoulder. Eventually gave up, relationship remained fractured until two performed intense scene focusing on fractured relationship between characters they portrayed. Reconciled as Ruby understood mother's feelings, vowed not to abandon friends as Ai did.

Mem-Cho: Member of idol group. Recruited by Aqua after LoveforReal performance, Mem's notoriety as online personality greatly enhanced group's fame. Despite Mem being 25 upon admission (way past ripe age for idol), Ruby accepts because they share same childhood dream. Ruby looks up to her, comments how she was cutie when first met. Both optimistic hard workers, propelling friendship further.

Pieyon: Long acquaintances through latter's affiliation with Ichigo Production, Inc. Finds working with him joy, appears one of few co-workers she genuinely respects—propelled him to silence Kana when she doubted his popularity.

Shun Yoshizumi: Met while working as reporter of Dig Deep! One Chance. Ambiguous if truly cares or sympathizes with him—being nice mainly to use him as investment for career per Ichigo's advice (be kind to assistant director to build relationship, hoping Shun might become main director future). Shun mistakes Ruby's friendliness as him being her type. Later after scandal on show, Ruby invited Shun to become manager—he accepts.

Friends:

Frill Shiranui: Classmate and friend. Ruby at first terrified to approach such famous person but broke ice after Aqua approached on her behalf. Eventually became friends over shared interest in LoveforReal. Often seen bantering with Ruby and Minami. Later worked together for The 15 Year Lie.

Minami Kotobuki: Classmate and friend. Often seen bantering with Ruby and Frill. Once accompanied Ruby to visit Aqua during Tokyo Blade stage adaptation rehearsals. Ruby later invited her to take part in cosplay segment of Dig Deep! One Chance.

Akane Kurokawa: First took note of Akane cast alongside brother on LoveforReal. Later subconsciously uttered "mama" upon seeing footage of Akane pretending to adopt Ai's persona. As Akane became brother's girlfriend, seen following Akane's account. Aqua told Ruby beforehand they only had professional relationship—caused Ruby to ruminate how scummy guys like him worst for not taking "cute" girlfriend like Akane seriously. Vowed to be nice to Akane when finally meet face to face.

At airport for Miyazaki trip, ecstatic finally meeting Akane in person. Instantly captivated by looks, praised Akane's beauty and cuteness. Akane returned gesture while humble, complimenting Ruby as much prettier than herself—caused Ruby to beam in delight. Elated over praise, asked if she can call her "sis." Shared always wanted older sister, questioned Akane when officially marrying Aqua to become sister-in-law. Earnestly asked Akane to take care of incompetent brother, whether marrying him.

At Takachiho, euphoric as Akane agreed sharing room. Began singing merrily about sleepover. Shared how familiar with "this place," how significant to her. Invited Akane to join B-Komachi; Akane apprehensive lacking necessary idol skills. In return, Akane asked if interested becoming actress, offered to guide. Ruby delighted but said would do so after fulfilling idol dream.

Changed subject, asked Akane about views on age gap. Akane replied mental state and age matter most, fine with 10-year gap. Followed with question about reason for topic—Ruby chuckled. Confessed has crush, history behind said crush to Akane, stating "sensei" gave purpose, without him wouldn't be able to live.

Akane empathized, stated having someone loves is good, little age gap won't matter in face of true love. Offered help for pursuit but Ruby explained unaware where he's gone. Ruby trusts Akane enough revealing all embarrassing advances she once made, only to be rejected. Her most captivating features are her pink-ruby eyes, which contain distinctive, star-like highlights—a trait that seems to fluctuate in intensity and color depending on her mental state and level of performance. Whether wearing her Youtou High School performing arts uniform or elaborate stage costumes, her visual charisma is often noted to be overwhelming.

Personality: In stark contrast to her calculated and gloomy twin brother, Ruby is extroverted, optimistic, and loud. She is highly communicative and socially aggressive, capable of making connections quickly, though she often lacks a verbal filter. While she utilizes an "airhead" persona to navigate the entertainment industry, she possesses a keen intuition. Her disposition is generally sunny, but she harbors a deep, obsessive drive regarding her family and her career. This drive can lead her to ruthlessness; while she began with a "pure" outlook, she has shown a willingness to utilize manipulative tactics and darken her own character to achieve her goals and find the truth she seeks.

Backstory: Born in secret to the top idol Ai Hoshino and raised within the care of Ichigo Production, Ruby’s early life was marked by the tragedy of her mother’s murder at the hands of a stalker. Raised by her adoptive parents, Ichigo and Miyako Saitou, she sought to follow in Ai's footsteps, eventually reviving her mother's idol group, B-Komachi. Unknown to the general public, Ruby is the reincarnation of Sarina Tendouji, a young girl who died of a terminal illness while under the care of a doctor named Gorou. Now blessed with a healthy body, she lives her second life with a ferocity intended to fulfill the dreams she couldn't achieve previously, all while hunting for the mastermind behind the destruction of her family.

Special Details: Ruby possesses a unique "star quality" that is literalized in her eyes; initially present in her left eye, she eventually awakens a second star in her right eye as her presence in the industry grows. This radiance is a double-edged sword, capable of turning dark and heavy when her emotions spiral. Despite being the daughter of a genius idol, her singing ability was initially quite poor, though her dancing talent and natural ability to attract fans are exceptional.

Age: 22

Occupation: Award-winning Actor (Lala Lai Theatrical Company)

Weight: Undisclosed

Height: Undisclosed

Appearance: Taiki often presents a relaxed and somewhat unkempt image, characterized by disheveled black hair and purple eyes inherited from his mother. He is typically seen wearing square-rimmed glasses and occasionally sports light stubble. However, his appearance undergoes a dramatic transformation when he prepares for a role; once groomed and his hair is tamed, his striking physical resemblance to his half-brother, Aqua Hoshino, becomes undeniable.

Personality: In his daily life, Taiki is notably laid-back and seemingly indifferent to social expectations or academic rigor—famously admitting he never bothered to learn how to read kanji. While some peers describe him as an "idiot trying to look cool," he possesses a complex personal code, particularly regarding his private life and relationships, to avoid the mistakes of his father. This casual exterior is a mask for his professional intensity; when acting, he completely immerses himself in his role, possessing a fierce, unshakable pride in his ability to dominate the stage.

Backstory: Taiki’s early life was defined by a hidden tragedy. Born Taiki Uehara, he was the product of an affair between his mother, Airi Himekawa, and a young man named Hikaru Kamiki. This secret led to a violent murder-suicide involving his mother and his legal father, Seijuro Uehara, when Taiki was very young. After spending time in an orphanage, he was taken in and raised by Toshirou Kindaichi of the Lala Lai Theatrical Company. It was only during his adult career that a DNA test revealed his blood connection to the Hoshino twins.

Special Details: Taiki is considered a prodigy in the theatrical world. A unique quirk of his craft is his refusal to wear contact lenses on stage; he believes that an actor can convey everything necessary through movement alone, even if he can only see the general shapes of his co-stars. He bought a luxury car and inmediately crashed it, it costed 3 commercials, needless to say he won't buy another one for a while because he's scared.

Taiki Himekawa - Relationships

Family:

Seijuro Uehara (Legal Father): Doesn't remember much, still young at time of death. Operating under mother's surname implies he holds him in contempt, not wanting association with murderer. Opinion fell lower upon learning he has half-brother, believing father had other children behind mother's back. Didn't realize it was actually other way around—mother cheated on father, prompting him to kill them both.

Not until hired for The 15 Year Lie that Taiki finally learned truth regarding parents' murder-suicide. Agreeing to play father in movie implies he sees him in new light now.

Airi Himekawa (Mother): Doesn't remember much, still young at time of death. Operating under her family name (Himekawa) implies he prefers her over murderous legal father. Not aware mother was child molester who conceived him when cheating on husband with 11-year-old boy.

Finally learned truth about mother when hired for The 15 Year Lie, which autobiographies her crimes. Caused views to change drastically—primary motivation for performing in movie being to make peace with her crimes. While understanding she was likely molested herself when younger, claims mother was responsible for own actions.

Lala Lai Theatrical Company:

Toshirou Kindaichi: Somewhat of father figure—looked after Taiki following parents' death.

Akane Kurokawa: Colleagues at Lala Lai but rarely shown interacting. On speaking terms—Taiki aware of Akane's admiration of Kana during childhood. Akane speaks to him during investigation of Aqua's father.

Others:

Kana Arima: First met participating in Tokyo Blade stage adaptation. Seems to respect her, asked for advice on reading Kanji (he can't). Told her not to hold back when acting together, asked her out for meals during filming breaks. Shown disapproval—scolded her for constantly fighting with Akane Kurokawa, stated if he knew she'd use book of Akane's career as ammunition he never would've lent it.

Melt Narushima: First met for Tokyo Blade stage play. Due to sharing many scenes, spent lots of time together but most interactions not shown. Worked together again for The 15 Year Lie—evident they've become rather close.

Frill Shiranui: Worked together on multiple projects before The 15 Year Lie. Get along well—he invites her on road trip to show off new car, doesn't take offense when she mocks him in front of others.

Other Relatives:

Aqua Hoshino (Half-Brother): First met during Tokyo Blade rehearsals, had several interactions. Taiki chastised Aqua over love triangle with Akane Kurokawa and Kana Arima, told him to just make choice already.

Didn't interact seriously until Aqua discovered through DNA analysis they share same biological father. Upon showing proof of blood connection, Aqua coerced Taiki into telling everything about father. Since Taiki didn't know he's product of affair, ended up setting Aqua on false lead revealing father Seijuro Uehara already deceased. After finding out truth, relationship grew—start acting like typical siblings with Taiki calling Aqua "little bro" knowing it annoys Aqua.

Upon learning of Aqua's death, Taiki was devastated, attended half-brother's funeral.

Ruby Hoshino (Half-Sister): When learned Aqua was half-brother, likely realized he has half-sister in Ruby. Worked together during The 15 Year Lie but no off-screen interactions shown. After screening finished and actors went to beach to celebrate, Taiki peeked at Ruby in swimsuit—Melt called him out for staring at relative but claimed not to care.

Hikaru Kamiki (Biological Father): Relationship basically non-existent—not aware he's illegitimate child born when mother molested latter while only 11 years old. Later found out truth about lineage when agreed to take part in The 15 Year Lie, which autobiographies mother's crimes. After Hikaru supposedly killed Aqua and found to be instigator of multiple homicide cases including his parents, opinion of biological father now likely reached rock bottom.

Age: Unknown

Occupation: Top-tier Fitness YouTuber, Professional Idol Choreographer and Producer

Weight: Undisclosed (Muscular build)

Height: 190 cm (6'3") — including mask

Appearance: Pieyon is a physically imposing, heavily muscled man with a deep tan. He is almost never seen without his signature yellow "cute bird" mask, a character design borrowed from a children's television program. He is incredibly disciplined, often staying in character for hours during grueling video shoots to maintain the "Pieyon" brand. He is pragmatic about the business of fame but remains a supportive and encouraging mentor.

Leveraging this expertise along with his passion for fitness, he signed with Ichigo Production and launched a YouTube channel that skyrocketed in popularity. He eventually became the agency's highest-grossing talent, proving that a unique gimmick backed by professional knowledge is a recipe for massive success.

Special Details: He is a financial powerhouse, reportedly earning over 100 million yen annually. He maintains a close relationship with the management at Ichigo Production and has a high level of trust with Aqua Hoshino—going so far as to allow the young man to use his "Pieyon" persona to help train others while the real Pieyon was away on vacation.

Timeframe: Post-Graduation / Movie Release
Duration: < 1 Week (Climax)
Estimated Dates: Spring 2026 (Twins’ Age: 18/19)

This is a powerful pivot for the story. Incorporating Tsukuyomi (the "Crow Girl") adds that supernatural, "fated" element that Oshi no Ko weaves into its most pivotal moments. It shifts the ending from a tragedy to a story of "Grace and Second Chances."

Here is the rewritten entry, formatted for your Lorebook with Recursion-Safe Keys:
File: The Final Arc (The Miracle)

Subject: Towards the Stars and Dreams
Timeframe: The End of Vengeance

    "The plan required a monster to kill a monster... but the gods demanded a different ending."

The culmination of Aqua’s life. Following the release of the movie 15-Year Lie and the successful dismantling of Hikaru Kamiki's reputation, the final physical confrontation occurred. Aqua, consumed by a need for atonement, believed his own death was the only way to truly end the cycle of blood.

In a desperate final move, Aqua cornered Kamiki on a cliffside. To ensure the threat was permanently removed, Aqua tackled his father over the edge and into the churning sea below. As the darkness of the water took him and his lungs began to fail, the supernatural entity known as Tsukuyomi intervened.
